Description: Materialized access-log table. Contains one row per facility access event (gate/door entry attempts), enriched with contact, facility, and organisation context. Row-level security enforced via a BigQuery Row Access Policy on org_id. Published atomically from an RLS-protected staging table so the previous protected version remains available until cutover; see includes/refresh.js.
The access code entered for the entry attempt.
The tenant who triggered the access event. Joins to contact.contact_id.
Timestamp when the record was created in the system.
The name of the access control device (e.g., gate keypad, door reader).
The type of access event (e.g., entry, exit).
The facility where the event occurred. Joins to facilities.facility_id.
Name of the facility where the event occurred. Denormalized from facilities.
Unique identifier for the access log entry.
Timestamp when the access event occurred.
The organization identifier. Common filter field across all views.
Name of the organization that owns the facility. Denormalized.
Additional detail about the result, particularly for denied access attempts.
The outcome of the access attempt (e.g., granted, denied).
Timestamp when the record was last updated.

Materialized auctions table. Contains one row per auction event (typically lien auctions for delinquent tenants) with facility and organisation attribution. Row-level security enforced via a BigQuery Row Access Policy on org_id. Published atomically from an RLS-protected staging table so the previous protected version remains available until cutover; see includes/refresh.js.
The deadline by which the auction must be advertised, as required by lien law.
Unique identifier for the auction.
Timestamp when the auction record was created.
Scheduled date and time of the auction.
The facility hosting the auction. Joins to facilities.facility_id.
Name of the facility hosting the auction. Denormalized from facilities.
The organization identifier. Common filter field.
Timestamp when the auction record was last updated.

Materialized book-entry table. Contains one row per accounting book entry (charges, payments, credits, and transfers), enriched with facility, lease, unit, and contact context. The pre-calculated amt_* columns make it easier to aggregate common financial metrics. Row-level security enforced via a BigQuery Row Access Policy on org_id. Published atomically from an RLS-protected staging table so the previous protected version remains available until cutover; see includes/refresh.js.
The last date of the period this entry covers (e.g., the end of the rent period for a rent charge). NULL for entries that do not cover a period.
The date from which this entry accrues (relevant for rent charges).
Name of the manager/user who created the journal entry, as shown in 'Added by' on the ledger. NULL for entries not created by a user.

External ID (user_...) of the manager/user who created the journal entry. May be absent from managers, which lists only the org's own managers (e.g., Cubby call-center staff are not included). NULL when added_by is NULL.
The monetary amount of the entry.
Portion allocated to assets on the balance sheet.
Portion allocated to liabilities.
Portion of the amount allocated to payments received.
Portion of the amount allocated to revenue.
Portion allocated to transfers between accounts.
References another entry this one applies to (e.g., a payment applying against a specific charge).
Categorizes the entry within accounts receivable (e.g., rent, fees, insurance).
The accounting book/ledger this entry belongs to (e.g., A/R).
Unique identifier for the book entry. Primary key.
The tenant/contact for this entry. Joins to contact.contact_id.
The tenant's name. Denormalized from contact.
Lease discount this entry is attributed to, where applicable. Joins to discounts.discount_id.
The datetime of the accounting entry.
Sequential entry number within a transaction.
Short code or label describing the entry type.
Human-readable description of the entry.
Name of the facility. Denormalized (note: same as facility_name in other tables).
The facility this entry belongs to. Joins to facilities.facility_id.
The fee this entry charges or waives, for fee entries. NULL otherwise.
The name of the fee (e.g., Late Fee, Admin Fee). Use with fee_id to break fee revenue down by fee.
For an entry that waives, reverses or adjusts an earlier charge (mostly waivers), the original charge entry. Joins to book_entries.book_entry_id. NULL otherwise.
For insurance entries, the coverage amount of the policy being charged. NULL otherwise.

Flag (0/1) for the journal entry: 1 when a person posted it (any entry a staff user makes, and every payment except an autopay charge, including tenant portal payments), 0 for automated postings such as recurring rent, scheduled fees and autopay.
Description of the journal entry this entry belongs to, as shown on the ledger.
The journal entry (transaction) this entry belongs to. All entries posted together in one transaction share this ID. Matches journalEntryId in the External API.
The lease this entry is associated with. Joins to leases.lease_id.
The organization identifier. Common filter field.

The payment transaction that created this journal entry (payments, refunds, failures). Joins to payments.payment_id. NULL for entries not created by a payment. On payment entries, lease_id is on the ACCOUNT_RECEIVABLE/PREPAID_RENT lines, not the payment-method lines.
The merchandise product sold, for retail entries. Joins to product.product_id. NULL otherwise.
Number of units sold, for retail entries. NULL otherwise.
The tax category applied to this entry.
Flag (0/1) indicating whether this entry is tax-exempt.

Internal numeric ID of the journal entry; matches 'Transaction #' shown on the ledger. Kept for existing queries; new queries should use journal_entry_id (matches the External API and other external IDs). May be deprecated in a future release.
The type of ledger entry - CREDIT/DEBIT
The unit name. Denormalized.
The unit associated with this entry. Joins to units.unit_id.

Materialized call-agent-availability table. Aggregates manager status durations by day and status for call-center availability reporting. One row per manager per availability status per day (bucketed by America/NY time zone). Row-level security enforced via a BigQuery Row Access Policy on org_id.
The date for which availability is recorded, bucketed by America/New_York (US Eastern).
The manager/agent whose availability is recorded. Joins to managers.manager_id.
The manager's name. Denormalized from managers.
The organization identifier. Common filter field.
Human-readable availability status name (e.g., Available, On Call, Offline).
The raw status code from the phone system.
Total seconds the agent spent in this status on the given day. Interval is attributed in full to the day it started in

Materialized call-child table. Contains one row per child call interaction — a single inbound call may have multiple legs (e.g., IVR, transfer to agent). Enriched with abandonment logic, facility context, assigned manager details, and a customer-facing call script with recorded Patty action telemetry. Use for granular call routing and agent-level analysis. Row-level security enforced via a BigQuery Row Access Policy on org_id. Published atomically from an RLS-protected staging table so the previous protected version remains available until cutover; see includes/refresh.js.
Whether the caller hung up before the call was answered by an agent (true/false)
The type of agent handling this leg (e.g., human, bot/IVR).
Timestamp when this leg was answered.
Unique identifier for the child call leg.
The parent call this leg belongs to. Joins to calls.call_id.

Customer-facing script-style rendering of the call leg. Contains a [CALL METADATA] line, an optional [TRANSCRIPT] status line, timed [MM:SS] or [HH:MM:SS] Caller/Patty dialogue lines for Patty calls when transcription is available, and a final [RECORDED PATTY ACTIONS] line sourced from recorded Patty action telemetry.
Whether this leg is inbound or outbound.
Duration in milliseconds of this call leg.
The facility associated with this call leg. Joins to facilities.facility_id.
The facility name. Denormalized from facilities.
TRUE when a recording is stored for this call leg (same rule the app uses for its hasRecording flag). Open it in the manager app at /calls/records/{call_id}.
The manager who handled this leg, if human. Joins to managers.manager_id.
The manager's name. Denormalized.
The organization identifier. Common filter field.
Timestamp when the parent call started. Denormalized from calls.started_at.
JSON object containing AI-scored quality metrics for this call leg.
Timestamp when this specific leg started.
Outcome/status of this call leg (e.g., answered, no-answer, transferred).
JSON object containing the transcription of this call leg.
Seconds the caller waited before this leg was answered.

Materialized calls table. Contains one row per inbound or outbound phone call, enriched with facility and organisation context. Row-level security enforced via a BigQuery Row Access Policy on org_id. Published atomically from an RLS-protected staging table so the previous protected version remains available until cutover; see includes/refresh.js.
Unique identifier for the call.
The phone number of the caller.
Name of the marketing (tracking) number the call came in on, captured when the call was received. NULL when the call did not come through a named marketing number. See marketing_numbers.
Whether the call is inbound or outbound.
Timestamp when the call record was created in the system.
Timestamp when the call ended.
The facility associated with this call. Joins to facilities.facility_id.
The facility name. Denormalized from facilities.
The phone number the call was forwarded from, if applicable.
The IVR menu option the caller selected (e.g., new_rental, existing_tenant, pay_bill).
The organization identifier. Common filter field.
Pipe-delimited list of outcome tags for the call, sorted alphabetically (e.g., autopay_enabled|payment_executed). A call can have several outcomes. NULL when none are tagged.
Disposition purpose tag for the call (e.g., sales_call, existing_customer_service_call). One value per call; NULL when the call has not been tagged. Populated from both manual and AI tagging.
The phone number that was dialed (the facility's tracking number).
Timestamp when the call started.
Overall status/outcome of the call (e.g., completed, missed, voicemail).
AI-generated summary of the call, written when the app scores the call from its transcript. NULL when no summary was produced (e.g., unanswered or untranscribed calls).
The support/tracking phone number this call was routed through.
Pipe-delimited list of topic tags for the call, sorted alphabetically (e.g., autopay|payment). A call can have several topics. NULL when none are tagged.
Timestamp when the call record was last updated.

Materialized contacts table. Contains one row per contact (tenant, lead, or prospect), enriched with first interest. A contact may have multiple leases over time. Row-level security enforced via a BigQuery Row Access Policy on org_id. Published atomically from an RLS-protected staging table so the previous protected version remains available until cutover; see includes/refresh.js.
Street address line 1.
Street address line 2.
City of the contact's address.
Company name, if the contact is a business tenant.
Unique identifier for the contact. Primary key.
Country of the contact's address.
Timestamp when the contact was created in the system.
The contact's date of birth.
The contact's email address.
The contact's preference for email communications (ALL_UPDATES or DO_NOT_DISTURB).
Whether the contact has self-identified as active military or a veteran.
The marketing source from which this contact originally came.
Current status of the contact in the lead pipeline (e.g., new, qualified, converted).
The contact's full name.
The organization identifier. Common filter field.
The contact's primary phone number.
An optional secondary phone number for the contact.
The contact's preference for SMS communications (ALL_UPDATES, SYSTEM_UPDATES, or DO_NOT_DISTURB).
State/province of the contact's address.
Timestamp when the contact record was last updated.
Postal/ZIP code.

Materialized Cubby events table. Contains one row per event (e.g., door locked, task changed, competitor tracked, pricing updated) with resolved organisation, facility, manager, unit, contact, and pricing-group context. Useful for operational auditing. Row-level security enforced via a BigQuery Row Access Policy on org_id. Published atomically from an RLS-protected staging table so the previous protected version remains available until cutover; see includes/refresh.js.
The contact associated with this event, if applicable. Joins to contact.contact_id.
Timestamp when the event occurred.
Serialized payload containing event-specific detail data.
The facility where the event occurred. Joins to facilities.facility_id.
Timestamp of the manager's most recent login at the time of the event.
The lease associated with this event, if applicable. Joins to leases.lease_id.
The manager who triggered the event. Joins to managers.manager_id.
The manager who triggered the event. Denormalized.
The organization identifier. Common filter field.
The pricing group associated with this event, if applicable. Joins to pricing_group.pg_id.
The product ID associated with this event, if applicable. Joins to product.product_id.
The type of action taken within Cubby (e.g., door_locked, task_changed, competitor_tracked).
The unit associated with this event, if applicable. Joins to units.unit_id.
Timestamp when the event record was last updated.

Materialized customer-touches table. Contains one row per customer touchpoint, linking GA session data to contacts and leases to attribute marketing source at the individual customer level. Enriched with contact, lease, lead, and organisation context. Row-level security enforced via a BigQuery Row Access Policy on org_id. Published atomically from an RLS-protected staging table so the previous protected version remains available until cutover; see includes/refresh.js.
The specific action the customer took (e.g., form_submit, checkout_started).
The contact who performed this action. Joins to contact.contact_id.
Timestamp when the touch was recorded.
The Google Analytics session identifier for this touch. Joins to ga_events via ga_session_id.
Google Click ID from a paid search ad click, if applicable.
The lead associated with this touch, if applicable. Joins to leads.lead_id.
The lease associated with this touch, if applicable. Joins to leases.lease_id.
The organization identifier. Common filter field.
The marketing source/channel of this touch (e.g., google, direct, email).
Calendar date dimension from 1900-01-01 through 2200-12-31. One row per date.
The calendar date. Primary key.
Integer representation of the date in YYYYMMDD format, useful for numeric comparisons and partitioning.

Date of the first day of the quarter containing this date.

Date of the first day of the year containing this date.
Whether the date is the first day of its month.
Whether the date is January 1st.
Whether the date is the last day of its month.
Whether the date is December 31st.
Whether the date matches today's date at the time the data was last refreshed.
Whether the date falls on a Monday through Friday.
Whether the date falls on a Saturday or Sunday.
Date of the last day of the month containing this date.
Date of the last day of the quarter containing this date.
Date of the last day (Saturday) of the week containing this date.
Date of the last day of the year containing this date.
Full name of the month (e.g., January).
Abbreviated month name (e.g., Jan).
Month number within the year (1–12).
Full name of the quarter (e.g., Q1).
Quarter number within the year (1–4).
Week number within the year (1–53).

Year and month formatted as a string (e.g., 2024-01), useful for monthly grouping.
Year and quarter formatted as a string (e.g., 2024-Q1), useful for quarterly grouping.

Materialized delinquency-exemptions table. Contains one row per active delinquency exemption: a manager-set hold that pauses some or all of a delinquent lease's collections steps until an end date. Matches the app API: exemptions that were removed, replaced or have expired are not included. Row-level security enforced via a BigQuery Row Access Policy on org_id. Published atomically from an RLS-protected staging table so the previous protected version remains available until cutover; see includes/refresh.js.
The tenant on the lease. Joins to contacts.contact_id.
Timestamp when the exemption was created, in facility local time.
Unique identifier for the exemption. Primary key.
The date the exemption ends, as entered. Can briefly be in the past until the app's expiry job removes the exemption.
The facility of the lease. Joins to facilities.facility_id.
The facility name. Denormalized.
Whether automated collections messages to the tenant are paused.
Whether late and delinquency fees are paused for this lease.
Whether the lease is held back from becoming lien-eligible (the path to auction).
Whether the overlock step is paused for this lease.
The lease the exemption applies to. Joins to leases.lease_id. A lease has at most one active exemption.
The manager who created the exemption. Joins to managers.manager_id.
The manager's name. Denormalized.
The manager's note attached to the exemption. NULL when none was entered. The same note also appears in manager_notes.
The organization identifier. Common filter field.
Free-text explanation, required when reason is OTHER. NULL otherwise.
Why the exemption was granted: BANKRUPTCY, DECEASED, MILITARY_SERVICE, PAYMENT_ARRANGEMENT or OTHER.
Timestamp when the exemption was last updated, in facility local time.

Materialized discount-programs table. Contains one row per discount program (e.g., Military Discount, Web Special, First Month Free) with organisation attribution. Row-level security enforced via a BigQuery Row Access Policy on org_id. Published atomically from an RLS-protected staging table so the previous protected version remains available until cutover; see includes/refresh.js.
Flag (0/1) indicating whether the program is currently active.
The discount value (percentage or dollar amount, depending on application_method).
How the discount is applied (e.g., percent, flat_amount).
Whether the discount applies to recurring rent or a one-time charge.
Timestamp when the program was created.
Unique identifier for the program. Joins to discounts.discount_program_id.
The name of the discount program.
When the discount begins (e.g., immediately, after a delay).
Number of months the discount is applied.
The organization identifier. Common filter field.
The name of the organization offering this program. Denormalized.
Number of months after move-in before the discount activates.
The type/category of discount program.
Timestamp when the program was last updated.
Number of free months granted under this program.
Number of months the tenant must pay upfront to qualify for this program.
Flag indicating whether the upfront requirement enforces payment of a full month's rent.

Materialized discounts table. Contains one row per applied lease discount, with its terms, facility context, and the discount program it was created from (NULL for discounts not created from a program). Discount configurations reflect the terms applied to this lease's discount, captured when it was applied. Row-level security enforced via a BigQuery Row Access Policy on org_id. Published atomically from an RLS-protected staging table so the previous protected version remains available until cutover; see includes/refresh.js.
Flag (0/1) indicating whether this discount is currently active on the lease.
The discount value, interpreted according to application_method. NULL for PAID_UPFRONT discounts.
How application_amount is applied to the charge (e.g. PERCENT_DEDUCTED, AMOUNT_DEDUCTED, AMOUNT_FIXED, NULL for PAID_UPFRONT discounts).
The lease's billing cycle when the discount was applied (MONTHLY, DAYS_28, WEEKLY, BI_WEEKLY).
The type of charge the discount applies to: RENT or FEE.
Timestamp when the discount was applied to the lease.
Customer-facing name of the discount, if one was set. NULL when no separate display name was set (most discounts).
Unique identifier for the discount. Primary key. Joins to book_entries.discount_id.
Name of the discount as applied to this lease. Captured when the discount was applied. Appears in book_entries.explanation_text on the discount's ledger entries.
The discount program this discount was created from. Joins to discount_programs.discount_program_id. NULL when the discount was not created from a program (about 22% of discounts).
Current name of the discount program this discount was created from. Denormalized from discount_programs. NULL when discount_program_id is NULL.
For PERIODIC discounts, when the discount begins relative to move-in: NOW, NEXT_MONTH, SPECIFIC_MONTH, NULL for other discount types.
The discount structure (e.g. PERIODIC, PERPETUAL, PAID_UPFRONT, ONE_TIME).
The original number of months the discount lasts, set when the discount was applied. Populated for PERIODIC discounts only.

Billing periods remaining on the discount. Counts down each time the discount is applied; 0 once it has been used up. Measured in billing_cycle periods (e.g., weeks for a WEEKLY lease). For the original length, see discounted_months.
The date the discount period ends on the lease.
The facility this discount is at. Joins to facilities.facility_id.
Name of the facility. Denormalized from facilities.
The lease this discount is applied to. Joins to leases.lease_id.
The organization identifier. Common filter field.
The original number of months after move-in before the discount begins, set when the discount was applied.

Billing periods remaining before the discount begins. Counts down as the lease is billed; 0 once the discount has started. Measured in billing_cycle periods. For the original delay, see start_after_months.
The date the discount period begins on the lease.
Timestamp when the discount record was last updated.
For PAID_UPFRONT discounts, the number of free months granted when the prepayment is made. NULL for other discount types.
For PAID_UPFRONT discounts, the number of months the tenant must prepay to qualify. NULL for other discount types.
For PAID_UPFRONT programs, 1 if the prepayment must cover full calendar months to qualify. NULL otherwise.
When the discount can be applied (START_ONLY, ALL).

Materialized emails table. Contains one row per outbound email (e.g., late notices, move-in confirmations, rate change letters) with contact, lease, facility, and organisation context. Row-level security enforced via a BigQuery Row Access Policy on org_id. Published atomically from an RLS-protected staging table so the previous protected version remains available until cutover; see includes/refresh.js.
The full HTML or text body of the email.
The reason code or description for a bounce, if applicable.

The manager or system process that created/triggered the email.
Timestamp when delivery was confirmed. NULL if not yet delivered.

The reason for a send failure, if applicable.

The lease associated with this email, if applicable. Joins to leases.lease_id.
Timestamp when the email was first opened. NULL if not tracked or not opened.

The organization name. Denormalized.
The email address of the recipient.
The name of the email recipient.
Timestamp when the email was sent.
Delivery status of the email (e.g., delivered, bounced, opened, failed).
The email subject line.
Category/template tag identifying the type of email (e.g., late_notice, move_in_confirmation).
The unit name associated with this email. Denormalized.

Name of the workflow that sent this email. NULL when not sent by a workflow.
The workflow run that sent this email, when it was sent by an automated workflow. NULL otherwise. Emails, sms and tasks from the same run share this ID.

Country inferred from the visitor's IP address.

Links GA events to a specific operator/organization. Common filter field.
Traffic medium (e.g., cpc, organic, email).
Campaign name (equivalent to UTM campaign).
Traffic source (e.g., google, facebook, email).
